vulnerability.title: Django uploaded file names with dot segments allow directory traversal on save

fixed_releases.verified_content: At 3.1.9 django/core/files/utils.py defines validate_file_name, which rejects names that are not their own basename and rejects '', '.', '..'; UploadedFile._set_name calls it (line 51), Storage.get_available_name and generate_filename reject '..' path parts, and MultiPartParser.sanitize_file_name strips both separators and returns None for dot names. At 3.0.2 none of these checks exist.

fix_commits.message: [3.1.x] Fixed CVE-2021-31542 -- Tightened path & file name sanitation in file uploads.

vulnerability.category_l2: Uploaded file name sanitation: dot segments and platform path elements survive os.path.basename, so a crafted multipart filename becomes a traversal path when the file is saved through FileField/Storage

description: Django upload handling trusts that removing directory prefixes from a submitted file name makes it safe. At 3.0.2, MultiPartParser.IE_sanitize (lines 300-302) only strips up to the last backslash, so a Content-Disposition filename whose surviving final segment is '.' or '..' (for example '/tmp/..' or 'foo\\..') reaches the upload handler unchanged; a name such as '$.$.$' that get_valid_filename later normalizes to '..' is a second route. UploadedFile._set_name (lines 38-50) then applies os.path.basename at line 42, which returns '.' and '..' unchanged and, on POSIX, does not treat backslash as a separator; there is no rejection of empty names or dot segments anywhere in the 3.0.2 upload path (django/core/files/utils.py contains only FileProxyMixin). When the file is saved through a FileField, FileField.generate_filename joins upload_to with the name (django/db/models/fields/files.py lines 295-307) and Storage.generate_filename normpaths the result (django/core/files/storage.py lines 101-108), so a dot-segment name escapes the upload_to directory (default FileSystemStorage.safe_join still confines writes to MEDIA_ROOT). The 3.1.9 fix 25d84d64 adds django/core/files/utils.py::validate_file_name, which rejects names containing path elements and the names '', '.', '..'; calls it from UploadedFile._set_name and FileField.generate_filename; adds '..' checks to Storage.get_available_name and generate_filename; rejects those names in get_valid_filename; and rewrites sanitize_file_name (introduced by the earlier CVE-2021-28658 fix) to split on both '/' and '\\' and return None for dot names, keeping IE_sanitize as an alias.

critical_operation.code_excerpt:
def _set_name(self, name):
        # Sanitize the file name so that it can't be dangerous.
        if name is not None:
            # Just use the basename of the file -- anything else is dangerous.
            name = os.path.basename(name)

            # File names longer than 255 characters can cause problems on older OSes.
            if len(name) > 255:
                name, ext = os.path.splitext(name)
                ext = ext[:255]
                name = name[:255 - len(ext)] + ext

        self._name = name
critical_operation.description: The submitted upload name is only passed through os.path.basename (line 42). That call removes directory prefixes but returns '.' and '..' unchanged, does not treat backslash as a separator on POSIX, and does not reject empty names. The resulting name is stored on the UploadedFile and later joined with upload_to and normpath'ed by FileField/Storage, so a dot-segment name escapes the upload directory. The 3.1.9 fix adds validate_file_name at line 51, which rejects path elements and the names '', '.', '..'.

entry_point.description: MultiPartParser.parse processes a multipart/form-data request whose Content-Disposition filename is attacker-controlled (sanitized only by IE_sanitize at line 212 in 3.0.2).

source_crosscheck.notes: NVD and the GitHub advisory agree on the 7.5 HIGH CVSS 3.1 vector and on CWE-22 (GHSA also lists CWE-434); the CVE List v5 CNA record carries no metric and marks CWE n/a. Severity LEVELS do not fully agree: NVD also publishes a legacy CVSS 2.0 5.0 MEDIUM metric and Django's own 2021-05-04 advisory labels the issue 'low severity' per its policy, while every modern CVSS 3.1/4.0 metric is HIGH (7.5/8.7). The independent reviewer therefore set severity_consistent=false and the entry stays pending rather than coercing a level. The 3.1-branch fix 25d84d64 and its 3.1.9 release notes describe the same mechanism as the NVD/GHSA path-traversal classification, and the code diff confirms the missing dot-segment validation in 3.0.2. Overlap that must be weighed: CVE-2021-28658, fixed at the same snapshot by the 3.1.x commit cca0d981 (replacing MultiPartParser.IE_sanitize at django/http/multipartparser.py:300-302 with sanitize_file_name), covers the parser-level upload-name traversal; CVE-2021-31542 is the published follow-up that adds the model/storage-level validate_file_name gate and affects the built-in UploadedFile/FieldFile flow. The reviewer judged them different defects (different reporter, fix commit, release, files and validation layer; OSV/GHSA alias sets do not cross-reference), not the same root cause double-counted. The other previously promoted django entries cover SQL injection (CVE-2020-7471 StringAgg delimiter, CVE-2020-9402 GIS Oracle tolerance), memcached key collision/data leakage (CVE-2020-13254), intermediate upload/cache directory permissions (CVE-2020-24583/CVE-2020-24584), admin ForeignKeyRawIdWidget XSS (CVE-2020-13596), archive extraction (CVE-2021-3281) and the MultiPartParser sanitize issue (CVE-2021-28658); none shares this fix commit.

review.blocking_reason: severity_consistent=false: NVD publishes a legacy CVSS 2.0 5.0 MEDIUM metric and Django labels the issue low severity, while modern CVSS 3.1/4.0 levels are HIGH. Published levels differ, so the entry stays pending and no level is coerced.
independent_corrections_accepted: Severity levels do not all agree: NVD publishes CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH and a legacy CVSS 2.0 5.0 MEDIUM metric, and Django's 2021-05-04 advisory labels the issue low severity. All modern CVSS 3.1/4.0 metrics agree at HIGH, but severity_consistent is false under the per-level rule.

Duplicate-check category labels were wrong: CVE-2020-13254 is a memcached key-collision/data-leakage issue, CVE-2020-24583/24584 are upload/cache intermediate-directory permission issues, and CVE-2020-13596 is a Django-admin ForeignKeyRawIdWidget URL-encoding/XSS issue (the header-injection advisory is CVE-2021-32052). Distinctness still holds.

CVE-2021-28658 was omitted from the initial duplicate check. The reviewer judged it a different defect: parser-only fix cca0d981 in 3.1.8/3.0.14/2.2.20, different reporter, and its advisory says built-in upload handlers were not affected; CVE-2021-31542 hardens UploadedFile._set_name, FileField.generate_filename, Storage and get_valid_filename and does affect the built-in flow.

Mechanism wording was overbroad: forward-slash components are removed by os.path.basename and backslash components by IE_sanitize; what survives is a final '.'/'..' segment (e.g. '/tmp/..' -> '..', 'foo\\..' -> '..') or a name that get_valid_filename normalizes to '..' (e.g. '$.$.$').
Attribution: sanitize_file_name was introduced by the CVE-2021-28658 fix and 25d84d64 rewrites it, keeping 'IE_sanitize = sanitize_file_name' as an alias.

Affected-range sources diverge: GHSA/OSV says introduced 3.0 fixed 3.1.9 (includes 3.0.2), while PYSEC-2021-7 and the CVE description start at 3.1 and Django's security archive lists only 3.2/3.1/2.2; the snapshot is vulnerable by code inspection and by GHSA's range.
review.duplicate_check: The reviewer checked the listed prior Django entries: CVE-2020-7471 (SQLi via StringAgg delimiter), CVE-2020-13254 (memcached key collision/data leakage), CVE-2020-24583/CVE-2020-24584 (intermediate upload/cache directory permissions), CVE-2020-13596 (admin ForeignKeyRawIdWidget XSS). None shares CVE-2021-31542's upload file-name path-traversal root cause. It also checked CVE-2021-28658 (omitted by the initial claim): public 2021-04-06, same advisory title, fixed by MultiPartParser-only commit cca0d981 in 3.1.8/3.0.14/2.2.20, and its advisory says built-in upload handlers were not affected. CVE-2021-31542 (fix 25d84d64, releases 3.1.9/3.2.1/2.2.21) adds validate_file_name at UploadedFile._set_name, FileField.generate_filename and Storage, dot-segment rejection in get_valid_filename, and both-separator splitting in sanitize_file_name, affecting the built-in UploadedFile/FieldFile flow. Different reporter, fix commit, release, files and validation layer; OSV/GHSA alias sets do not cross-reference the two CVEs. Conclusion: related follow-up hardening, not the same root cause double-counted.

limitations: Static verification only; no Django application, multipart upload or storage write was performed.

Exploitation depends on the application saving the uploaded file through a FileField/FileSystemStorage path where a dot-segment name is preserved; the advisory's CVSS vector assumes network access with no privileges.
Only the 3.0.2 snapshot is analyzed; the advisory also covers the 2.2 and 3.2 lines with separate fix commits.
The CVE List v5 CNA record has no CVSS metric and marks CWE as n/a; the severity level is taken from NVD Primary and the GitHub advisory, which agree.

The advisory names MultiPartParser, UploadedFile and FieldFile; this entry records UploadedFile._set_name as the single root-cause location because it is the common gate for submitted names at 3.0.2, while the fix hardened all three.
No independent third-party reproduction reference is recorded, so grade A is not available.

NVD also publishes a legacy CVSS 2.0 5.0 MEDIUM metric and Django's advisory calls the issue 'low severity'; the independent reviewer set severity_consistent=false, so the entry is not promoted until the severity-level rule is clarified. Modern CVSS 3.1/4.0 levels are all HIGH.

Impact nuance: default FileSystemStorage.path() uses safe_join, so escaping MEDIA_ROOT is blocked; the reachable traversal on the default backend is from the upload_to subdirectory to sibling paths, while custom/non-filesystem storages are not protected by safe_join.
open_questions: Whether 3.0.2's multipart parser can deliver a bare '.' or '..' filename on every upload handler path was checked statically only; no runtime upload was attempted.

Whether the dataset should treat CVE-2021-31542 (follow-up fix) as a distinct entry from CVE-2021-28658 (original parser-level fix), given that both are present at the same 3.0.2 snapshot and share the uploaded-name traversal primitive.
